newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease as investors eye election.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease as investors eye election.

text.p: Slovenian shares inched lower on Wednesday as investors hesitated to take on positions before the country's general elections on Sunday, and traders said the downward trend could well continue for the rest of the week.

"Foreign investors are not as active as they were, they are probably waiting for the elections and the listings of some newly privatised companies like port company Koper and petrol trader Petrol," said one trader.
The SBI index fell 0.78 percent or 9.29 points to 1,179.6. Overall 11 shares fell, four rose and one was unchanged, while another eight were untraded.

Turnover rose to 200.6 million tolars from 92.6 million, but traders said volumes were expected to remain light because of the reluctance of foreign investors, the key players on Slovenia's fledgling bourse.
Drug producer Lek's A issue was the most actively traded, falling 0.97 percent to 20,400 tolars on volume of 5,820 shares for total turnover of 118.6 million tolars.
Financial consultancy Dadas was the day's biggest gainer, firming 9.19 percent to 13,900 tolars on volume of 88 shares.
"Dadas most probably rose in a reaction to yesterday's steep fall. I think there was too much panic around Dadas yesterday," said a market participant.

Brokerage Dadas was banned from trading on the Ljubljana bourse on Tuesday because of alleged illegal trading practices, but most traders said the widely expected ban had little effect on the overall market. Dadas' shares plummeted 37.7 percent on Tuesday.
Warehouse group BTC was the day's leading decliner, falling 5.23 percent to 12,310 tolars on volume of 342 shares. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
